importance_ranking.reason: High visual variation across sub-types — a guard cabin, site office, bunk house, and container-style cabin are visually distinct products. Buyers use the image to identify the correct product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Cabin size and wall panel type are the primary shortlisting criteria — a 10x8 ft GI-sheet cabin cannot substitute for a 40x10 ft PUF-panel site office. Buyers cannot evaluate fit without these specs visible on the listing.

Price varies substantially with cabin size and panel type — a guard cabin and a large site office are orders of magnitude apart. Indian B2B buyers compare prices aggressively across sellers once size and panel type are confirmed; listed price is the primary comparison lever.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Tata Steel MobiNest is a recognised brand with buyer recall in the premium segment; buyers in institutional and government procurement actively specify or prefer branded manufacturers.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer vs trader distinction matters for delivery to remote sites, installation capability, and after-sales support. Institutional and government buyers evaluate company track record during vendor selection.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Custom-dimension builds are additionally quoted per square foot by some manufacturers — sellers should clarify unit when quoting non-standard sizes, but per piece is universally understood for standard catalogue cabins.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece is entirely implied for standard catalogue-size cabins; no buyer questions whether a portable cabin is sold per piece. The per-sq-ft exception applies only to custom builds and is resolved in negotiation.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Size is the single largest price driver — a 40x8 ft site office costs multiples of a 10x8 ft guard cabin, and sizes are non-interchangeable across project requirements.
PUF panel vs GI sheet represents a significant price and thermal performance difference — non-interchangeable for climate-specific or comfort-grade requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Internal height determines habitability for accommodation and office use — standard 7 ft vs high-ceiling 9 ft is a meaningful differentiator affecting comfort, HVAC requirements, and price, but is not captured by the existing Cabin Size spec (which specifies length x width only).

top_rfq_specs.reason: Application routes the RFQ to sellers who supply the right cabin type — a security cabin manufacturer may not supply resort-room-grade accommodation cabins, and the application determines the feature set and finish level sellers need to assess fit and price.
Length is the primary size constraint sellers need to confirm manufacturing feasibility and provide an accurate price — it is the dominant dimension in Indian portable cabin sizing conventions.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need the panel type to determine material cost and thermal performance — a resort room or accommodation cabin in a hot climate requires PUF insulation while a basic site office may use GI sheet, and these have significantly different prices.

Sellers need to know whether electrical fittings are required to provide an accurate quote — a cabin with three-phase wiring and LED fittings is priced substantially differently from a bare structure with no electrical.
